structured_output.world_model:
W1 (mechanism), after E028.

**Tip: E027**
- E026 math cut to 8.75 true epochs (219 steps at batch 2000), with 20/24/28/32 px at 0/15/40/70% of steps.
- Score: 5.878 s and 0.7547 on seeds 0–2. The held-out mean is 0.7526, below the bar. The real margin is negative by about 0.05 pp, so the next time cut needs an accuracy booster first.

**Noise**
- Any change to the trajectory (LR, LS, alpha, step count) reshuffles the 3-seed mean by about ±0.3 pp.
- The held-out 10-seed SE is about 0.1 pp.
- Effects under about 0.2 pp cannot be read even on held-out seeds.

**Time model**
- Time is about steps × pixel fraction × 27 ms, plus about 0.25 s of fixed cost.
- Moving 15% of steps from 24 to 20 px saves about 0.17 s.
- Scalar changes (LR shape, LS, Lookahead interval, alpha) are time-neutral within ±0.03 s.
- FreezeOut (E028): −9% time for about −0.2 to −0.3 pp. That is about the epoch-dial rate, not better.

**Accuracy mechanisms**
- Every scalar optimizer or regularization knob tried so far has been flat within noise: LS, Muon lr, wd, LR floor, alpha exponent.
- Accuracy is set by the late 28/32 px high-capacity phase plus Lookahead averaging.
- Re-timing the warm-up, the Lookahead interval, or late LS = 0 are more knobs of the same kind. I expect ±0.1 pp, with no booster of 0.15 pp or more.
- Per-resolution whitening fixes a stem mismatch that BN and the whitening bias already absorb. I expect a small effect.
- Early 20 px is only cheap while LR is below its peak (peak at 23% of steps). Extending 20 px to 30% puts it into the peak-LR window, so it should cost about 0.1–0.3 pp.

**Strategy**
- The only remaining cuts are of the same kind (epochs, early resolution, freezing), and all cost about 0.2–0.3 pp per 10% of time.
- Without a real booster, the tip is near the Pareto edge. Further gains probably need a structural change, such as a different architecture or step efficiency.

forecasts.reason: Peak timing is a scalar schedule knob. Every knob of this kind has been flat, and an earlier peak puts peak LR in the 20 px phase, so I expect a held-out change under 0.15 pp.
With the total pull per step held fixed, the reset interval barely changes the averaging that sets the end-point. E025's loss came from pull strength, not the interval.
Dropping LS late sharpens logits but removes regularization in the under-fit CIFAR-100 regime. E013 showed LS is flat, so I expect a net change of about 0.
The extra 20 px steps fall in the warm-up and peak window, where features are less disposable than in the first 15%. Expect −0.17 s and about −0.1 to −0.2 pp held-out, close to the 0.15 pp threshold.

The BN after group 1's conv and the trained whitening bias already absorb the stem's statistical mismatch. The 32 px tail sets the final features, so the gain should be under 0.15 pp, with a small extra prepare cost.

cruxes: Does any time-neutral change move the held-out mean by at least 0.15 pp? If none of I047, I048, I049 or I051 does, the tip is at the Pareto edge and further time cuts need a structural change, not scalar tuning.
Is the accuracy cost of a 20 px step set by its position relative to the LR peak (before vs. after 23% of steps)? I050's held-out result settles whether early resolution is still a cheap dial.

How far is the PCIe judge's 40-seed mean from local held-out seeds? If it transfers within 0.1 pp, a held-out mean of about 0.752 is safe against the official 0.75 bar, and about 0.2 pp of margin can be spent on time.
